paragraphs.title: The Happiness of Those Who Follow Torah

answers: Those who walk in the law of the LORD
easy.explanation: Verse 1 says, “Blessed are the undefiled in the way, who walk in the law of the LORD.”
easy.q: Who are called blessed at the beginning of the passage?

easy.explanation: Verse 2 says they “seek him with the whole heart.”
easy.q: How do those who seek the LORD seek him?

easy.explanation: Verse 8 says, “I will keep thy statutes.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist promise to keep?

medium.explanation: The opening verses connect wholehearted seeking with walking in God’s ways.
medium.q: What connection does the passage make between seeking God wholeheartedly and walking in His ways?

answers: That his ways may be directed to keep God’s statutes
That he may depart from God’s law
medium.explanation: He asks that his ways be directed so he will not be ashamed.
medium.q: What does the psalmist ask so that he will not be ashamed?

answers: Those who walk faithfully in God’s law
medium.explanation: The phrase is explained by “who walk in the law of the LORD.”
medium.q: What does “undefiled in the way” mean in context?

answers: Blessing, obedience, a request for steadiness, and praise
challenge.explanation: The psalm moves from blessing to keeping God’s statutes and asking for a steadfast way.
challenge.q: Which sequence of ideas appears in these verses?

answers: So he can keep God’s statutes faithfully
So he can leave the law
So he will not need to learn
challenge.explanation: The request is directly connected with keeping God’s statutes.
challenge.q: Why does the psalmist ask that his ways be directed?

answers: It is joined with sincerity and praise
challenge.explanation: The psalmist will praise God with an upright heart after learning His righteous judgments.
challenge.q: What does “uprightness of heart” show about learning God’s judgments?

short_answers.question: What is the central blessing in verses 1–3?
short_answers.answer: Walking faithfully in the law of the LORD.
short_answers.explanation: The opening describes those who walk in God’s ways as blessed.

short_answers.question: What does the psalmist ask for in verse 5?
short_answers.answer: That his ways may be directed to keep God’s statutes.
short_answers.explanation: He asks for steadiness so that he may obey.

short_answers.question: How does the section end?
short_answers.answer: With a promise to keep God’s statutes and a plea not to be forsaken utterly.
short_answers.explanation: Verse 8 combines commitment with dependence on God.

answers: By taking heed according to God’s word
easy.explanation: Verse 9 gives this answer directly.
easy.q: How may a young man cleanse his way?

easy.explanation: Verse 11 says, “Thy word have I hid in mine heart.”
easy.q: Where did the psalmist hide God’s word?

easy.explanation: Verse 12 says, “teach me thy statutes.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask God to teach him?

answers: That he might not sin against God
That he could conceal it from everyone
medium.explanation: Verse 11 gives the purpose: “that I might not sin against thee.”
medium.q: Why did the psalmist hide God’s word in his heart?

answers: To make one’s conduct pure through obedience to God’s word
medium.explanation: The verse explains cleansing as taking heed according to God’s word.
medium.q: What does it mean to cleanse one’s way?

answers: He declares them with his lips
medium.explanation: Verse 13 says, “With my lips have I declared all the judgments.”
medium.q: What follows the psalmist’s learning of God’s judgments?

answers: The heart stores God’s word, the lips declare it, and memory guards against forgetting
They are all described as obstacles
challenge.explanation: The psalmist hides the word in his heart, declares it with his lips, and promises not to forget it.
challenge.q: How do heart, lips, and memory work together in this passage?

answers: He values them as greatly as great riches
challenge.explanation: Verse 14 compares his joy in the testimonies with all riches.
challenge.q: What does rejoicing in God’s testimonies show?

answers: To understand and follow His ways
To find a way around them
challenge.explanation: Meditation is joined with having respect unto God’s ways.
challenge.q: What is the purpose of meditating on God’s precepts?

short_answers.question: How can a young man cleanse his way?
short_answers.answer: By taking heed according to God’s word.
short_answers.explanation: Verse 9 identifies obedience to the word as the means of cleansing.

short_answers.question: Why is God’s word hidden in the heart?
short_answers.answer: So the psalmist will not sin against God.

short_answers.question: What does the psalmist promise not to forget?

answers: That God deal bountifully with His servant
easy.explanation: Verse 17 asks God to deal bountifully with His servant so that he may live.
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask in order that he may live?

easy.explanation: Verse 18 says, “Open thou mine eyes.”
easy.q: What does he ask God to open?

answers: A delight and a source of counsel
easy.explanation: He calls the testimonies his delight and the statutes his counsellors.
easy.q: What are God’s testimonies and statutes to the psalmist?

answers: Because he is a stranger in the earth and needs guidance
Because he wants to forget them
medium.explanation: Verse 19 joins his condition as a stranger with his request for instruction.
medium.q: Why does the psalmist ask that God’s commandments not be hidden from him?

answers: He accepts the ways of the wicked
He has no interest in them
medium.explanation: His soul breaks for the longing it has unto God’s judgments at all times.
medium.q: What does his longing for God’s judgments show?

answers: He feels temporary and dependent on divine direction
medium.explanation: The statement leads to his request that God not hide His commandments.
medium.q: What does “I am a stranger in the earth” suggest here?

answers: It gives delight, counsel, and discernment against the proud
It keeps him away from all people
challenge.explanation: God’s testimonies delight him and His statutes serve as counsellors while the proud reproach him.
challenge.q: How does Torah protect the psalmist in this passage?

answers: God’s testimonies guide and advise him
challenge.explanation: The testimonies function as a source of counsel.
challenge.q: What does “my counsellors” mean in context?

answers: He wants to behold the wondrous things in God’s law
challenge.explanation: Verse 18 explicitly connects opened eyes with seeing wondrous things out of God’s law.
challenge.q: Why is the request to open his eyes appropriate?

short_answers.question: What does the psalmist ask God to do to his eyes?
short_answers.answer: Open them to behold wondrous things out of God’s law.

short_answers.question: How does the psalmist describe himself?
short_answers.answer: As a stranger in the earth.

short_answers.question: What are God’s testimonies to him?

easy.explanation: He asks, “quicken thou me according to thy word.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask when his soul cleaves to the dust?

easy.explanation: Several verses repeat his request to be taught God’s statutes.
easy.q: What does he ask God to teach him?

easy.explanation: Verse 29 says, “Remove from me the way of lying.”
easy.q: What does he ask to have removed?

answers: He asks God to teach him His statutes
medium.explanation: After declaring his ways, he says, “thou heardest me: teach me thy statutes.”
medium.q: What does the psalmist do after declaring his ways?

answers: He is weakened by deep sorrow
medium.explanation: The phrase describes intense emotional distress.
medium.q: What does “my soul melteth for heaviness” mean?

medium.explanation: Verse 32 says he will run when God enlarges his heart.
medium.q: What will enable him to run in the way of God’s commandments?

answers: From dust and heaviness toward understanding, truth, and obedience
challenge.explanation: The psalmist asks for quickening, understanding, removal of falsehood, and strength to obey.
challenge.q: What movement of the soul appears in the passage?

answers: Faithfulness gives him confidence not to be ashamed
It makes him conceal his faith
challenge.explanation: He says, “I have stuck unto thy testimonies: O LORD, put me not to shame.”
challenge.q: How is sticking to God’s testimonies related to shame?

answers: A deliberate choice of faithfulness over falsehood
A choice of wealth over Torah
challenge.explanation: He asks to have lying removed and declares that he has chosen the way of truth.
challenge.q: What does the movement from lying to truth signify?

short_answers.question: What does the psalmist ask when his soul cleaves to the dust?
short_answers.answer: That God quicken him according to His word.

short_answers.question: What does he ask God to remove?
short_answers.explanation: He asks for freedom from falsehood in verse 29.

short_answers.question: What will allow him to run in God’s commandments?
short_answers.explanation: Verse 32 gives the condition for this freedom and energy.

easy.explanation: Verse 33 begins, “Teach me, O LORD, the way of thy statutes.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask God to teach him?

easy.explanation: He asks for his heart to be inclined to God’s testimonies and not to covetousness.
easy.q: Toward what does he ask God to incline his heart?

easy.explanation: Verse 37 says, “Turn away mine eyes from beholding vanity.”
easy.q: What does he ask God to turn away?

answers: Understanding helps him keep God’s law with his whole heart
Understanding causes him to leave the law
medium.explanation: He asks for understanding and then promises to keep and observe the law wholeheartedly.
medium.q: What connection does the passage make between understanding and obedience?

medium.explanation: It is set opposite God’s testimonies as a misplaced desire for gain.
medium.q: What does “covetousness” mean in this context?

answers: God’s servant devoted to His fear
medium.explanation: Verse 38 speaks of “thy servant, who is devoted to thy fear.”
medium.q: For whom does the psalmist ask God to establish His word?

answers: Turning from vanity helps him live according to God’s way
The eye has no connection with conduct
challenge.explanation: The psalmist asks God to turn his eyes from vanity and quicken him in His way.
challenge.q: How does the passage connect sight with integrity?

answers: The psalmist trusts that God’s judgments will protect him from shame
challenge.explanation: He asks God to turn away reproach because His judgments are good.
challenge.q: Why are God’s good judgments connected with removing reproach?

answers: Instruction, purified desire, mercy, and life
challenge.explanation: The prayers ask for understanding, freedom from vanity, mercy, and quickening.
challenge.q: Which combination of needs appears in the passage?

short_answers.question: What does the psalmist ask God to teach him?
What does he reject in favor of God’s testimonies?
short_answers.explanation: He asks God to incline his heart away from covetousness.

short_answers.question: What does he ask God to turn his eyes away from?
short_answers.explanation: Verse 37 identifies vanity as the object he wants to avoid.

easy.explanation: Verse 41 asks for God’s mercies and salvation according to His word.
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask to come to him?

answers: An answer based on God’s word
easy.explanation: He asks for God’s word so he may answer him that reproaches him.
easy.q: What will he have with which to answer the reproacher?

easy.explanation: Verse 46 says, “I will speak ... before kings, and will not be ashamed.”
easy.q: Will he speak of God’s testimonies before kings without shame?

answers: Because he trusts in God’s word
medium.explanation: Verse 42 says, “for I trust in thy word.”
medium.q: Why can the psalmist answer the reproacher?

answers: The faithful message he does not want removed from his mouth
medium.explanation: He asks not to have the word of truth taken utterly from his mouth.
medium.q: What is “the word of truth” in context?

medium.explanation: He lifts his hands toward the commandments he loves and meditates in God’s statutes.
medium.q: What does lifting his hands toward God’s commandments express?

answers: God’s mercy and salvation give him a basis for answering and speaking truth
challenge.explanation: After asking for salvation, he describes answering reproach and speaking before kings.
challenge.q: How does salvation produce courage?

answers: Love gives him courage to speak of them openly
challenge.explanation: Because he delights in and loves the commandments, he will not be ashamed to speak of them.
challenge.q: How is love for God’s commandments related to freedom from shame?

answers: Mercy, trust, truth, and faithful obedience
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from seeking mercy to trusting God’s word, speaking truth, and keeping the law.
challenge.q: What progression appears in the verses?

short_answers.question: What does the psalmist ask to come to him?
Why can he answer the reproacher?
short_answers.answer: Because he trusts in God’s word.

short_answers.question: Where will he speak of God’s testimonies?
short_answers.explanation: Verse 46 says he will speak before kings without shame.

easy.explanation: Verse 50 says, “This is my comfort in my affliction: for thy word hath quickened me.”
easy.q: What comforts the psalmist in his affliction?

easy.explanation: He says, “yet have I not declined from thy law.”
easy.q: Did the psalmist depart from God’s law when the proud mocked him?

easy.explanation: Verse 55 says, “I have remembered thy name ... in the night.”
easy.q: When did he remember God’s name?

medium.explanation: The word is explicitly called the psalmist’s comfort and source of life.
medium.q: How does God’s word act during affliction?

answers: The temporary place where he lives as a traveler
medium.explanation: The phrase describes his temporary earthly dwelling.
medium.q: What is “the house of my pilgrimage”?

medium.explanation: Verse 55 ends, “and have kept thy law.”
medium.q: What followed his remembering God’s name at night?

answers: God’s word gives life, and God’s statutes become songs
challenge.explanation: God’s word quickens him, while His statutes are his songs in the house of pilgrimage.
challenge.q: How are joy and life connected in this passage?

answers: He remains faithful despite social pressure
challenge.explanation: The proud mock him, yet he does not decline from God’s law.
challenge.q: What does perseverance under mockery show?

answers: Keeping them is presented as the reason for his comfort and songs
challenge.explanation: He says his comfort and songs are connected with God’s word and statutes, and that he has kept the precepts.
challenge.q: How are keeping the precepts and comfort related?

short_answers.question: What is the psalmist’s comfort in affliction?
What did the proud do to him?
short_answers.answer: They had him greatly in derision.

short_answers.question: When did he remember God’s name?

paragraphs.title: Examining the Way and Hurrying to Obey

easy.explanation: Verse 57 says, “Thou art my portion, O LORD.”
easy.q: Who is the psalmist’s portion?

answers: He turned his feet to God’s testimonies
easy.explanation: Verse 59 says he turned his feet unto God’s testimonies.
easy.q: What did he do after thinking on his ways?

easy.explanation: Verse 63 calls him a companion of all who fear God.
easy.q: With whom does the psalmist claim companionship?

medium.explanation: He thinks on his ways and turns back to the testimonies.
medium.q: What does examining his ways represent?

medium.explanation: The next phrase, “and delayed not,” clarifies the meaning.
medium.q: What does “I made haste” mean here?

medium.explanation: The verse joins fearing God with keeping His precepts.
medium.q: Why is companionship with those who fear God appropriate?

answers: Reflection, return, haste, and fellowship with the faithful
challenge.explanation: These ideas appear in sequence throughout the passage.
challenge.q: What sequence describes the correction of his way?

answers: Choosing God leads him to resolve to keep His words
The choice causes him to leave them
challenge.explanation: Verse 57 connects the LORD as his portion with his commitment to keep His words.
challenge.q: How does choosing the LORD as his portion relate to keeping His words?

answers: It shows that God’s mercy is widespread while the psalmist asks for instruction
It shows that he gives up
challenge.explanation: The final verse praises God’s widespread mercy and asks Him to teach His statutes.
challenge.q: What does “the earth is full of thy mercy” add to the passage?

short_answers.question: Who is the psalmist’s portion?
What did he do after thinking on his ways?
short_answers.answer: He turned his feet to God’s testimonies.

short_answers.question: What does he say about the earth?
short_answers.answer: It is full of God’s mercy.

easy.explanation: Verse 65 says, “Thou hast dealt well with thy servant, O LORD.”
easy.q: How had the LORD dealt with His servant?

easy.explanation: Verse 66 asks for good judgment and knowledge.
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask God to teach him?

easy.explanation: Verse 72 gives this comparison.
easy.q: What is better to him than thousands of gold and silver?

medium.explanation: He says that after being afflicted he kept God’s word.
medium.q: What did the psalmist learn after going astray?

medium.explanation: It is paired with knowledge and learning God’s commandments.
medium.q: What does “good judgment” mean here?

answers: He kept God’s precepts with his whole heart
medium.explanation: Verse 69 records his wholehearted obedience.
medium.q: What did he do despite the lie forged against him?

answers: As circumstances through which he can learn God’s statutes
challenge.explanation: He says it was good that he was afflicted so that he might learn God’s statutes.
challenge.q: How are afflictions presented in the passage?

answers: It is worth less than riches
challenge.explanation: The psalmist expressly values God’s law above thousands of gold and silver.
challenge.q: What does the comparison with gold and silver teach about the law?

answers: He moves from going astray to keeping the word and preferring God’s law
He moves from obedience to forgetfulness
He moves from Torah to wealth
challenge.explanation: The section describes correction through affliction and a renewed preference for God’s law.
challenge.q: What change appears from the early verses to the end?

short_answers.question: How had God dealt with His servant?
short_answers.answer: He had dealt well with him.

short_answers.question: What did affliction teach the psalmist?
short_answers.explanation: Verse 71 says affliction helped him learn them.

short_answers.question: What is better than thousands of gold and silver?

easy.explanation: Verse 73 says, “Thy hands have made me and fashioned me.”
easy.q: Who made and fashioned the psalmist?

easy.explanation: The passage contains requests for understanding, comfort, and tender mercies.
easy.q: What does he ask for after affliction?

easy.explanation: Verse 74 says those who fear God will be glad.
easy.q: Who will be glad when they see the psalmist?

answers: So he may learn God’s commandments and testimonies
So he can forget the law
medium.explanation: He repeatedly asks for understanding in order to learn God’s commandments.
medium.q: Why does the psalmist ask for understanding?

answers: Merciful kindness that strengthens and encourages him
medium.explanation: He asks for God’s merciful kindness to be for his comfort.
medium.q: What does “comfort” mean in this passage?

answers: They dealt perversely with him without a cause
medium.explanation: Verse 78 describes their wrongful treatment.
medium.q: What did the proud do to the psalmist?

answers: After suffering, he hopes that those who fear God will turn to him
He wants to withdraw from everyone
challenge.explanation: He asks that those who know God’s testimonies turn to him.
challenge.q: How are affliction and fellowship connected?

answers: A desire to abandon the statutes
challenge.explanation: He asks for a sound heart so that he will not be ashamed.
challenge.q: What does a sound heart in God’s statutes express?

answers: They are requested as the source of renewed life
challenge.explanation: Verse 77 asks for tender mercies so that he may live.
challenge.q: How do God’s mercies relate to life?

short_answers.question: Who made and fashioned the psalmist?
Who will be glad when they see him?
What kind of heart does he ask for?
short_answers.answer: A sound heart in God’s statutes.
short_answers.explanation: He asks for this so that he will not be ashamed.

easy.explanation: Verse 81 says, “My soul fainteth for thy salvation.”
easy.q: For what does the psalmist’s soul faint?

easy.explanation: He says, “I hope in thy word.”
easy.q: What does he hope in?

easy.explanation: Verse 83 says he does not forget God’s statutes.
easy.q: What has he not forgotten?

medium.explanation: He asks when God will execute judgment on those who persecute him.
medium.q: What does the psalmist ask God to execute against his persecutors?

answers: A leather container dried and shriveled by smoke
medium.explanation: The image describes his worn and diminished condition.
medium.q: What is a bottle in the smoke?

answers: Pits that were not according to God’s law
medium.explanation: Verse 85 says the proud dug pits for him.
medium.q: What did the proud dig for him?

answers: Hope in God’s word and continued obedience
challenge.explanation: Although persecuted, he continues to hope in God’s word and does not forsake His precepts.
challenge.q: What sustains the psalmist when he is nearly consumed?

answers: The persecutors act wrongfully, while God’s commandments are faithful
The persecutors are faithful and the commandments persecute
challenge.explanation: He calls all God’s commandments faithful and says he is persecuted wrongfully.
challenge.q: What contrast appears between the persecutors and God’s commandments?

answers: So he may keep the testimony of God’s mouth
So he may abandon the law
challenge.explanation: He asks for life so that he can continue keeping God’s testimony.
challenge.q: Why does he ask to be quickened at the end?

short_answers.question: For what does the psalmist’s soul faint?
What does he hope in?
short_answers.explanation: He repeats this hope in verses 81 and 83.

short_answers.question: What does he ask God to do for his persecutors?

answers: In the house of the wicked
easy.explanation: Verse 89 says, “For ever, O LORD, thy word is settled in heaven.”
easy.q: Where is God’s word settled forever?

easy.explanation: Verse 90 says God established the earth and it abideth.
easy.q: What did God establish so that it abides?

easy.explanation: Verse 93 says, “with them thou hast quickened me.”
easy.q: What has quickened the psalmist?

answers: Both are presented as enduring and established
medium.explanation: God’s word is settled forever, and the earth stands by His establishment.
medium.q: What connection does the passage make between God’s word and the earth?

medium.explanation: The statement contrasts finite things with the exceeding breadth of God’s commandment.
medium.q: What does “an end of all perfection” mean?

medium.explanation: The psalmist says he would have perished unless God’s law had been his delights.
medium.q: What does God’s law provide in affliction?

answers: Finite things end, but God’s commandment is exceedingly broad
God’s commandment is more limited than all things
challenge.explanation: Verse 96 contrasts the limits of created things with the breadth of God’s commandment.
challenge.q: What does the contrast between an end and the broad commandment teach?

answers: It remains firm, delights the afflicted, and quickens the servant
challenge.explanation: The passage joins the permanence of the word with the psalmist’s life and delight.
challenge.q: How does God’s word provide both life and comfort?

challenge.explanation: His belonging is expressed alongside his seeking of God’s precepts.
challenge.q: Why can the psalmist say, “I am thine”?

short_answers.question: Where is God’s word settled forever?
What did God establish?
short_answers.explanation: Verse 90 says the earth was established and abides.

short_answers.question: What is exceedingly broad?

paragraphs.title: Torah as a Source of Wisdom

easy.explanation: Verse 97 begins, “O how love I thy law!”
easy.q: What does the psalmist love?

easy.explanation: Verse 98 says God’s commandments make him wiser than his enemies.
easy.q: What does God’s commandment give him against his enemies?

easy.explanation: Verse 104 says, “therefore I hate every false way.”
easy.q: What way does he hate?

medium.explanation: Verse 99 gives his meditation on God’s testimonies as the reason.
medium.q: Why does the psalmist have more understanding than his teachers?

medium.explanation: Verse 103 compares God’s words with honey.
medium.q: What does “sweeter than honey” describe?

answers: Keeping and meditating on them give him understanding
medium.explanation: He gains understanding through God’s precepts and therefore hates false ways.
medium.q: How are keeping the precepts and understanding related?

answers: Love, meditation, and obedience to God’s law
challenge.explanation: The psalmist attributes his wisdom to constant meditation and keeping God’s precepts.
challenge.q: What is the source of wisdom in this passage?

answers: God’s instruction exposes the evil of false ways
challenge.explanation: Understanding through the precepts leads him to hate every false way.
challenge.q: Why does rejecting falsehood follow understanding God’s precepts?

answers: The sweetness and desirability of God’s words
challenge.explanation: The comparison expresses the psalmist’s delight in God’s words.
challenge.q: What does the comparison with honey emphasize?

short_answers.question: What does the psalmist love?
What makes him wiser than his enemies?
short_answers.explanation: Verse 98 attributes his wisdom to them.

short_answers.question: What does he hate?

easy.explanation: Verse 105 says, “Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.”
easy.q: What is God’s word compared to?

easy.explanation: Verse 106 says he will perform God’s righteous judgments.
easy.q: What does the psalmist swear to perform?

answers: Quicken him according to God’s word
easy.explanation: Verse 107 asks God to quicken him according to His word.
easy.q: What does he ask God to do when he is afflicted?

answers: They guide his feet and path
medium.explanation: The verse directly identifies the feet and path as what the word illuminates.
medium.q: What is the function of the lamp and light?

answers: His life is constantly in danger
medium.explanation: The expression describes vulnerability and danger.
medium.q: What does “my soul is continually in my hand” suggest?

medium.explanation: Verse 108 asks, “teach me thy judgments.”
medium.q: What does he ask God to teach him after offering his mouth’s freewill offerings?

answers: God’s word guides the way in which he keeps his oath
challenge.explanation: The illuminated path is the path of God’s righteous judgments that he vows to keep.
challenge.q: How is the light connected with the oath?

answers: He does not go astray because he remains faithful to God’s precepts
challenge.explanation: Though the wicked lay a snare, he says he erred not from God’s precepts.
challenge.q: What does his resistance to the snare show?

answers: He asks to be quickened so he can continue keeping them
challenge.explanation: He asks for life according to God’s word and then asks to be taught His judgments.
challenge.q: Why are righteous judgments connected with life?

short_answers.question: What is God’s word to the psalmist’s feet?
What did he swear to perform?
What does he ask God to teach him?

easy.explanation: Verse 113 says, “thy law do I love.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist love?

easy.explanation: He says, “I hate vain thoughts.”
easy.q: What does he hate?

easy.explanation: Verse 114 says, “Thou art my hiding place and my shield.”
easy.q: Who is his hiding place and shield?

answers: Depart from him so he may keep God’s commandments
medium.explanation: Verse 115 asks evildoers to depart so that he may keep God’s commandments.
medium.q: What does the psalmist ask evildoers to do?

medium.explanation: The request is for support so that he may live safely.
medium.q: What does “uphold me” mean?

medium.explanation: Verse 116 says, “let me not be ashamed of my hope.”
medium.q: What does he ask not to happen because of his hope?

answers: Trust in God enables him to separate from evil and keep the commandments
The refuge leads him toward evil
challenge.explanation: Because God is his refuge and shield, he asks evildoers to depart while he obeys.
challenge.q: How does refuge in God relate to rejecting evildoers?

answers: God’s judgment removes the wicked like dross and produces fear
challenge.explanation: The passage describes God removing the wicked and causing the psalmist to fear His judgments.
challenge.q: What connection does the passage make between judgment and the wicked?

challenge.explanation: The imagery of dross removal emphasizes purity, leading to love for God’s testimonies.
challenge.q: Why does the psalmist love God’s testimonies after the wicked are removed?

short_answers.question: What does the psalmist love?
Who is his hiding place and shield?
What does he ask evildoers to do?
